prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Katy, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1294; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim documentation. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened.

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Katy, Texas, in the right lane. Traffic was moving normally before that.

Q: What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my head snapped forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle right away?

A: Yes, I got out and checked the car. The rear bumper was pushed in and the trunk wouldn't close properly.

Q: Did the other driver say anything at the scene?

A: He said he was looking at his phone and didn't see the light change back to green. He seemed apologetic.

Q: How are you feeling physically now?

A: My lower back is sore and stiff, especially when I sit for a long time or get out of bed in the morning. I've been taking over-the-counter pain relievers and using a heating pad.

Q: Have you seen a medical provider about it?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They diagnosed a back strain and gave me instructions for stretching and rest. I'm scheduled for a follow-up next week.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Just that I'm trying to keep up with work, but I've had to take a few shifts off because of the pain. I'd like to know what the next steps are for my repair and medical claims.

Q: Thank you. I'll follow up with you by mail with those details. Have a good day.

A: Thanks, you too.
